editorial:
You follow Travis Bickle, a lonely night-shift cab driver in New York, as his sleepless nights turn into dark thoughts and a need to clean up the city. The movie feels tense, gritty, and uncomfortable, pulling you into his lonely world without asking you to agree with him. You watch him drift through neon streets, talk to strangers, and slowly lose touch with normal life. The story is simple but heavy, and every scene makes you feel his isolation.

Robert De Niro gives a powerful performance, and the city looks rough and real. The pacing is slow at first but builds to shocking moments, so it may not be for everyone. The music and camera work keep you on edge, even when nothing big happens. It is not a fun movie, but it is unforgettable. If you like character studies and crime dramas, this is a must-watch.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Travis kills the men controlling Iris and rescues her. He tries to shoot himself but has no bullets left, then police arrive. Instead of being punished, the media treats him like a hero. In the last moment, he drives again and sees something in his mirror, suggesting his violent thoughts may not be gone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves intense character studies and classic crime dramas.
